author: Sangmin Kim
title: New event venue, fast-food restaurant proposed at southwest Bakersfield mansion: docs - NewsBreak
text:
By Sangmin Kim ,
5 hours ago
UPDATE: The Bakersfield Planning Commission unanimously approved the preliminary planning steps Thursday for a project proposing a new event center and other major structures at an existing mansion on Buena Vista Road.
BAKERSFIELD, Calif. (KGET) -- A new event venue, fast-food restaurant and other major additions are being proposed at the site of an 18,000-square-foot mansion in southwest Bakersfield, according to city documents.
The new property owner is proposing a new event center, 2,500-square-foot fast-food restaurant with a drive-thru window, and a convenience store with 16 fuel pumps -- all on 20 acres on Buena Vista Road, south of McCutchen Road.
Watch 'After Sunrise' on KGET+; Click to learn how to get KGET+ on your smart TV devices The newly proposed event venue would hold up to 250 to 300 guests and host up to 52 "large-scale" events per year. The existing home would also be used for smaller events, according to documents.
According to Patricia Newquist with Cornerstone Engineering, the developers for this project, the new event center will have "an emphasis on weddings, quinceañeras and family reunions."
The Bakersfield Planning Commission is scheduled to hold a public hearing on this project during its regular meeting Thursday.
According to the meeting agenda, the Commission could approve the proposed General Plan amendment and zoning change at this hearing. If approved, the Commission would recommend the Bakersfield City Council to do the same.
If the City Council also approves, the Commission would later consider other applications submitted by the property owner, including the conditional use permit.
Palazzo Destefani -- a mansion built in 2007 -- has been serving as an event venue in the past years, mainly for weddings.
In March 2022, an arsonist started a massive fire that destroyed a good portion of the property. Its assessed value at the time was $3 million.
Marty Sias was arrested the next morning after starting two more fires, one of which damaged Independence High School, according to officials. He was sentenced to 15 years in prison .
The meeting is set to begin at 5:30 p.m. at 1501 Truxtun Ave.
